findings.title: Free collateral cannot be derived from position and margin data; naive arithmetic misclassifies one wallet in five
findings.observation: withdrawable == accountValue - totalMarginUsed for 19% of wallets; 20% misclassified as able to defend
findings.sample: 74 Hyperliquid wallets holding open BTC positions, queried live 2026-08-20
findings.method: compare venue-reported `withdrawable` against marginSummary arithmetic on the same response
findings.confidence: single venue, single moment, wallets already known to hold positions; would be strengthened by repetition across days and by a second venue
findings.market_gap: no provider checked (HyperTracker, Coinglass, 0xArchive, Tardis, QuickNode, Dwellir, PurrData) exposes this field

findings.title: Order-book depth falls as price moves get larger, so a static-book cascade estimate is optimistic
findings.observation: depth after / depth before = 0.894 during moves of 0.475-1.271%, against 1.00 in quiet markets
findings.sample: BTCUSDT, 30 days of Binance bookDepth, 6,478 non-overlapping observations, largest bucket n=58 across 14 distinct days
findings.method: notional within +/-1% after a window divided by before, bucketed by absolute move, de-overlapped at the horizon
findings.confidence: 30 days only; the full 1,324-day run is running and will decide whether the extreme buckets survive
findings.market_gap: no liquidation product models a non-static book

findings.title: A properly aged wallet universe sees 53.3% of Hyperliquid BTC open interest, not 20%
findings.sample: 31,349-wallet universe; stratified estimate with a random sample of 1,200 of the 25,954 newly discovered wallets
findings.method: known stratum from the last deep scan plus mean-per-wallet extrapolation over the new stratum; bootstrapped interval
findings.confidence: still a lower bound — the universe is activity-derived and the recording keeps discovering wallets
findings.market_gap: no provider publishes a coverage figure for position data

findings.title: The wallet universe is exhausted; more wallets of the same kind would add nothing
findings.observation: claimed 20.24% coverage was near the ceiling; actual is 53.3%
findings.sample: the claim rested on a universe frozen after FOUR HOURS of recording, documented as 21 days
findings.method: n/a — the error was a premise never measured, not a calculation

findings.title: Daily-horizon directional tests on one instrument cannot detect realistic edges; the region is unpowerable, not empty
findings.observation: detecting a 52% hit rate needs 4,900 independent days (13.4 years); 51% needs 19,600 (53.7 years)
findings.sample: standard power arithmetic applied to the project's own recorded sample sizes
findings.method: 80% power, alpha .05 two-sided, on a proportion, with observations counted as INDEPENDENT rather than raw
findings.confidence: arithmetic, not an estimate; the only judgement is what effect size counts as realistic

findings.title: Binance order-book behaviour under stress transfers to Hyperliquid
findings.observation: none — nothing has been measured on Hyperliquid
findings.confidence: untested and load-bearing; hl2 began recording Hyperliquid l2Book at nSigFigs=3 on 2026-08-20 to settle it

findings.title: No provider sells per-wallet account state, so an archive of it is a durable moat
findings.observation: HyperTracker sells it — complete market coverage, 15-20 minute snapshots, history from 2025-04-04, $179-1,999/month
findings.method: n/a — the claim was asserted from landing pages rather than docs
findings.confidence: refuted from the vendor's own field list
